Rules summary Contents 1 Differences between the BGA implementation and the Physical game 1.1 1. Initial Captain, Cards and Resources selection 1.2 2. VP track 2 Game Overview 3 Core Concept: Icons & Eggs 4 Gameplay 4.1 1. Deploy Crew Member (Explore) 4.2 2. Play Cards (Expand Reserve) 4.3 3. Claim Achievement 4.4 4. Recharge (Reset) 5 End of Game & Scoring Differences between the BGA implementation and the Physical game 1. Initial Captain, Cards and Resources selection In the BGA implementation, you select the Captain you play, the cards you start with (4 out of 8) and your additional starting resources (unless you're the starting player) all at once. Once all players have made their selection its all revealed to the other players. If you follow the rules to the letter, selecting starting resources should happen after Captain + Card selection. This results in a faster set-up phase, and players can start playing more quickly. 2. VP track In the BGA implementation, your score marker will stop moving on the score track once it reaches 50 points. You can still gain additional points during the game but your marker wont move any further. Your score marker will always reflect your current VP value in side the marker. In the physical game you would take another lap around the track, but this can be confusing for some players as you don't gain additional bonuses from the track by taking another lap. Game Overview As explorers, we scout a mysterious island to discover rare creatures and settle them in our reserve. The game blends worker placement (crew members) with engine building (creature cards). The core mechanic is collecting icons on cards to fulfill scientific goals (Achievements). Core Concept: Icons & Eggs Icons: Each card in your reserve shows icons (e.g., Magnifier, Paw). These are required for achievements but are not spent . Eggs: These act as wild icons. When used for an achievement, flip them to the "hatched" side (they stay in your reserve but lose their wild property). Gameplay On your turn, perform exactly 1 of these 4 actions: 1. Deploy Crew Member (Explore) Place your crew member so it straddles the line between two hex tiles. Cost: Plains are free. Mountains cost 1 resource of your choice. Gain: From all adjacent habitats (hexes), you may EITHER take 1 resource OR take 1 matching creature card from the Wilderness (market) into your hand. Bonus: Collect all eggs on the two hexes covered by your crew member. Activate any action icons on those hexes. 2. Play Cards (Expand Reserve) Play up to 2 cards from your hand into your reserve. Cost: Pay the resources printed in the top-left corner of the card. Effects: "Instant" lightning bolts trigger once. "Permanent" infinity symbols are active from now on. "Recharge" icons only trigger during the "Recharge" action. 3. Claim Achievement Choose one of the 3 face-up achievements. Requirement: Your reserve must display all required icons (on cards or eggs). Reward: Take a trophy (victory points), place your marker, and unlock your Captain ability. You cannot play any more cards during this turn. 4. Recharge (Reset) Only possible if all 3 of your crew members are on the board. Retrieve: Return all figures to your supply. Time Stone: Advance the time stone. If it reaches an egg symbol, replenish eggs on the board and refresh the card market (Wilderness). Effects: Activate all cards in your reserve that have a "Recharge" icon. Hand limit: 5 . End of Game & Scoring The game ends when a player takes the last trophy and finishes their turn, and then every other player has taken one more turn. Final scoring adds points for the following: Creatures in your reserve with an end game ability Creatures in your reserve with an end game score Achievements 3 points per trophy 1 point for every 4 leftover resources and/or butterfly nets BGA always shows the cumulative instant score for all players (with a brown icon) during the game. If Live Scoring is enabled, you will also see the total score (with a red icon).

[Rating: 1/10] Game designers should be more careful with the publishers they choose for foreign languages. Spanish publisher barely provided copies to the stores.

[Rating: 1/10] Suffers from a serious "rich-get-richer" problem. You fall behind, there is no way to catch up.

[Rating: 2/10] Card Drawing the game...  Overall goal is to sift through an enormous pile of dreck cards to find useful ones.  Would have been better served with a third less cards, so that cards in the wilderness are all worthwhile.

[Rating: 3/10] I wanted to love this game, but what a slog it is. Any initial joy felt from the beautiful artwork and design is sucked up just past the midpoint of the game while you and everyone else is just hoping someone will finally end it.  It was a bit deja vue to Septima, another incredibly stunning work of art that you wanted to shoot yourself while playing.   Just too long for what is, it really overstays its welcome. At one point near the grind at the end I thought to myself, I think I'd rather be at work. Sweet begeezus, that has never happened!  I'm rating this a BGG 3.... "Bad- likely won't play

[Rating: 3/10] Too long and unsafisfying play with OP card combos. Nowhere near in comparison with Ark Nova and tries to overcompensate by the bling of it’s components/production.

[Rating: 3/10] Great art but very boring gameplay and super slow turns. I see there are a lot of high positive reviews for this game which makes me wonder if I'm missing something with my playthrough.  The constant appearance of the cards make downtime very problematic as players need to go through every card and compare it with the achievement to really optimize their tableau. The achievements are also poorly designed, since if you're beat to a certain achievement then the next unlock takes a much longer time to reach. It can hold you back from unlocking your hero for a long time.  Overall, cute art tableau

[Rating: 3/10] There is just too much going on in this game. There are so many different ways to score its hard to focus your strategy. The cards have so many different things they can do it can be hard to create good synergy. We finished the game and I felt like there was plenty of stuff left undiscovered (I suppose this could add to replay value). This game didn't seem to benefit from the point salad aspect. Trying to figure out what was going to score the most points was impossible because everything scores you points.
